calls: every call the recorder made to a product export (function, class constructor `new X`, instance method `X#m`) with its arguments viewed at call time, in order; an argument over 4000 bytes of JSON is stored once in the set `shared` table and referenced as {"$shared": n}
compare: mixdog-ai providers::openai pool.rs (:178-230 sessionless sockets), transport/ws.rs connect (:280-288 lookup): serve each case's `input.answers` per upgrade request and compare the ordered `events` (dial, upgrade request with every header, response or refusal, closes), the clock steps and the outcome (entry or error whole).

describedValues.{\"$instance\": name, constructedWith: [: an instance of a product class, as the arguments it was constructed with
describedValues.{\"$response\": {status, statusText, hea: a fetch Response handed to the product: status, headers (in order) and the body chunks as delivered (bytes)
describedValues.{\"$stream\": [chunk...]}: an async stream the recorder handed the product, as the chunks it yields in order
describedValues.{\"callback\": name}: a function the recorder handed the product; its scripted behaviour is the case body

entry: openai-ws-pool.mjs acquireWebSocket / releaseWebSocket (with openai-ws-connect.mjs openHedged inside, over the real ws client) against a loopback WebSocket server (lib/ws-world.mjs): a stuck upgrade is an upgrade request the server never answers; the hedge (3000 ms) and acquire deadline (15000 ms) run on the virtual clock, each step waiting for the dial it causes. cachedLookup is called directly (the host resolver). Not run: a live endpoint, a proxy.
exclusions: the server answers upgrade request n with input.answers[n-1] (null = never answered, absent = accepted); the 1006/terminate conventions are those of lib/ws-world.mjs
the DNS case resolves `localhost` through the host resolver: the addresses are the recording host's

no string is rewritten: the data directory is the fixed D:/mixdog-build/tmp/w22/<set> and the product tree D:/mixdog-build/tmp/b6f-tree (paths as Node produced them, Windows separators where Node wrote them): a replay maps its own temp directory to that prefix
net requests: x-stainless-os / -arch / -runtime-version and the user-agent of the SDK client stack carry the recording host's OS, architecture and Node version
net requests: the recorder's x-bench-origin header is left out and `host` is the host of the origin the product addressed (the loopback port is random)

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay: Rust entry (pub, on o1): mixdog_ai::providers::openai WsPool::checkout (openai/pool.rs:178) and mixdog_ai::transport::ws::connect (transport/ws.rs:237). There is no hedge or acquire deadline and no shared DNS resolution in Rust (K1 G6, G15): work for the Rust side.
values: exact (benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/lib/exact.mjs): every input, argument list, result and error is stored through the shared encoder; what JSON cannot hold is a {"$exact": <kind>} tag
